threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the Tube and not the underground. And don't get me started on your panic over the next strike.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the driver with an acoustic guitar, while a couple argued over whose turn it was to pay for the next round.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids trading Pokémon cards in the Spielplatz while their parents bartered for fresh produce at the nearby market—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: On Sundays, the lines at the flea markets stretch longer than the actual sales. It's a ritual here—scavenging for forgotten treasures while sipping beer.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they dodge the pigeons on Valencia. Tourists stop and gawk, but we know they’re just waiting to drop a bomb on your head.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus last night that was so packed, people were hanging on outside. Reminder that SF rush hour is just as wild as the nightlife.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell, but it's the small playgrounds like the one at Plaça del Sol where local kids spend their afternoons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll notice them struggling to pronounce ‘Gràcia’ like it’s spelled — locals drop the ‘cia’ and keep it quick. They’ve definitely just moved in.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep using the term 'the tube' instead of just 'the Overground' like a true local. It's cute, but it gives you away.
Last week on the 3 bus, a guy serenaded the driver with an old Brixton reggae tune. The driver actually smiled. That's London at night for you.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw an old man at the corner café arguing passionately with a pigeon over a croissant.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM, serving homemade sauces while the party crowd spills out into the street. It's a late-night rite.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the loud bang at Civic Center wasn't just another train issue, it's a regular drum solo from a guy who thinks he's the next big thing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a woman expertly juggle three bags while balancing on one foot to catch the 38. No one even flinched; just another Tuesday in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think all bars close at 2 AM, but the real locals know the best places often stay open way later, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stare at the metro map as if it's a treasure map, not realizing the best routes are often just one stop away.
